![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14173511/assets/b365c6a6ae3ff9320465fe9a69e55b1737a7ffedf6cf6da6e91a5ed4ace3ba38.png)

Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $PR=QR$ and $\overset{⟷}{RS}⊥\overset{―}{PQ}.$
question.worked_solution:
By the converse of the perpendicular bisector theorem, a point equidistant from the endpoints of a segment lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment. 

Here, the point $R$ is equidistant from the endpoints of $\overset{―}{PQ}.$ Therefore, $\overset{⟷}{SR}$ is the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{PQ}.$ 

In particular, we have that $SP=SQ.$ We can use this equation so solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}SP & =SQ \\ 8x-5 & =6x+1 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$
